Clerk pricing matrix: "Passkeys — Authenticate with any form of passkeys": not included on the Free plan, included on Pro and above; "Biometric sign-in — Let returning users sign in to native apps with their device's biometrics" is likewise a paid-tier feature.

Clerk site: "Bot Detection — Dramatically reduce fraudulent sign-ups with built-in, continually updated machine learning" and "Email and SMS one-time passcodes — Fast and reliable one-time passcode delivery with built-in brute force prevention."

Clerk site, Session Management: "Clerk manages the full session lifecycle, including critical security functionality like active device monitoring and session revocation" — with per-device sign-out ("Sign out of device") shown in the user profile UI.

Clerk pricing: the Free plan carries a "Machine Authentication — API Keys & M2M Tokens limit per month"; machine authentication (API keys and machine-to-machine tokens) is a metered platform feature across plans.

A user says Clerk tries to cram everything into its libraries (Web3, Stripe), and its JS blob now triggers browser inspector warnings for slow loading. Every React upgrade, Clerk libraries were the biggest pain because of transitive dependencies, including conflicting Stripe library versions. The libraries are obfuscated and the 'isomorphic' TS code is hard to debug.

The same user says Clerk lacks audit logs and versioning: someone changed a console setting and the team couldn't trace when it happened or who did it. They also had to wake up on a Sunday because Clerk API calls for token refreshes were failing.

"Clerk looks _really_ good initially. It's perfect if you want to prototype something and not care about auth." Problems appear in the details: there's still no offline auth on mobile, so the app can't be opened without connectivity. The commenter is switching their company to Logto.

Workaround for offline mobile auth: the team cached the credentials and the JWT refresh token from Clerk, then manually requested the access token through Clerk's sparsely documented frontend API. This required faking the cache API and pulling the token from the undocumented "__clerk_client_jwt" key. They say Better Auth supports this out of the box.

Using Clerk and quite unhappy. There's no proper RBAC: roles are tied to organizations rather than the user, so you can't have a global admin unless you store arbitrary key-value pairs in metadata. More than once in recent weeks or months, downtime caused the whole app to fail. Would think twice before using it again.
Clerk adoption seems to be becoming the norm in recent years. The commenter started using it about a year ago and found its reliability troublesome.

Recently switched from Clerk to BetterAuth and recommends it: it supports more of what they need, is more reliable, and is much cheaper. They originally chose Clerk because no open-source alternative existed and they wouldn't roll their own auth, but now see no reason to pick Clerk.
Better Auth is described as way more hackable than something like Clerk. The team added a plugin for auth via iframe postMessage (embedded in a CRM) and it worked seamlessly.

Better Auth stores all auth data in your own DB with one CLI command and includes OAuth providers (Google, Apple, GitHub) for free. "Not saying Supabase and Clerk are bad, but they cost money. With better auth you pay exactly $0."
"Man, glad I chose WorkOS instead. I've been a happy camper there but have wondered about Clerk bc it felt hotter. Turns out hot isn't always good."
A commenter warns against outsourcing auth to VC-funded vendors, saying they will eventually milk customers: "Clerk's pricing should be evidence enough."
"I think Clerk looks great but it starts to get quite expensive if MFA is a requirement."
"Clerk seems fine, Auth0 is fine, but I'd rather build on open-source."
"The Next.js integration story is already really quite good." The commenter also likes seeing a service focus on removing all the pain of user management, not just login.

Confused by launch pricing: free up to 5,000 MAU, but the paid tier is $49/mo for 1,000 MAU plus $0.05 per additional MAU. So going from 5,000 to 5,001 MAU jumps from $0 to $249/mo. The commenter also asks how MAU is calculated.

Security concerns at launch: clerk.dev and the dashboard scored poorly on securityheaders.com. Including third-party CDN JS (jsdelivr) without SRI on login pages for the dashboard and customer logins was called a red flag for security-critical apps.
